# Paravoxia — orchestration & token discipline

Fable weekly limits are the binding constraint; most spend is long-context
cache reads, not output. Every session in this repo follows these rules.

## Model tiering (frontmatter already set — don't override upward casually)

- **fable (inherit)**: `chapter-director`, `score-director`,
  `cinematography-director`, `story-alignment-judge`,
  `scene-cohesion-judge` — creative build and taste-critical judgment only.
- **opus**: `story-naive-reader`, `story-canon-auditor`, `story-verifier`,
  `scene-naive-viewer`, `cinematography-continuity-auditor`,
  `score-continuity-auditor`, `player-experience-auditor` — blind reading,
  auditing, and mechanical verification.
- Any ad-hoc Explore/general-purpose agent for searching, doc-reading, log
  triage, or probe-running: pass `model: "opus"` (or `"haiku"` for trivial
  greps). A mechanical subagent must never inherit fable.

## Main-session context hygiene

- Stay an orchestrator. Don't pull the design corpus (~65k tokens:
  `PARAVOXIA_PROGRESSION.md`, `PARAVOXIA_CH4_PLAN.md`, `main/STORY.md`) into
  the main context unless doing the creative work directly here — delegate
  reading to a subagent and keep only its conclusions.
- Verification (movie probes, screenshot strips, `npm run verify`) goes to
  `story-verifier`, not inline Bash loops. Run dev servers and long probes in
  the background; read back tails, never full logs.
- Guided-play changes require both the verifier's objective/marker/feedback
  lifecycle proof and a fresh read-only `player-experience-auditor` report.
  Neither role patches or substitutes for a creative director.
- After finishing a chapter or review, remind the owner to `/clear` before the
  next task; suggest `/compact` before starting a long build phase when
  context is already large.

## This machine runs concurrent sessions

Other agents and the owner work in this repo at the same time. Two incidents in
one session on 2026-09-04:

- A parallel refactor of `main/src/utils/fauna*.ts` landed mid-`verify` and made
  it fail on files the running session had never touched. **Before treating a
  gate failure as yours, check `ls -l` timestamps against your last edit.** Do
  not "fix" a module someone is actively splitting — you will collide with work
  whose destination only they know.
- A probe pointed at `127.0.0.1:5199` measured a DIFFERENT PROJECT after that
  port was taken over. It returned 200 and rendered a real app, so nothing
  looked wrong. **Probes must verify identity, not liveness** — check for
  `<title>Paravoxia</title>` before trusting a measurement. `npm run
  verify:visual` picks a free port and does this check; copy that pattern.

`npm run dev` fails here with `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers
reached` (the `captures/` tree is enormous). Use `npm run build` plus
`npx vite preview`.

Two more harness traps, both hit on 2026-09-04:

- **A background shell that waits with `until ! pgrep -f "<name>"` waits forever**,
  because the pattern matches the waiting shell's own command line. Use the
  bracket trick — `pgrep -f "[n]ame"` — or run dependent steps sequentially in
  one shell instead of polling.
- **Probes must own their server's lifetime.** Nine orphaned `vite preview`
  processes were left behind by probes that crashed. `tools/lib/previewServer.mjs`
  now kills the child on exit/signal; use it rather than spawning a preview by
  hand. Its `assertHardwareGl` check is also mandatory: without `--use-gl=angle`
  headless Chromium here silently used SwiftShader and a boot profile showed a
  20-second stall that the real GPU never produces.
- **Probe switches** (players never set these): `?worldprep=sync` forces the legacy
  synchronous world generation; `?beatregistry=off` serves the legacy story tables
  instead of beat contracts. Both exist so a baseline and a candidate come from ONE build.
- **Edit-then-measure ordering.** A build started 27 seconds after a source edit
  contains that edit. Capture a baseline BEFORE changing the code path it
  measures, or use the same-build A/B switches (`?worldprep=sync`,
  `?beatregistry=off`) so baseline and candidate come from one build.

## Creative triad

For any new scene, awakening, substantial cutscene recut, or audiovisual
polish pass, invoke the `creative-triad` skill. The Chapter, Score, and
Cinematography directors are peers. They communicate through the run's scene
contract and structured director notes; they do not race edits in shared
timeline files or approve their own implementation.

Chapter, Score, and Cinematography are exactly the three peer creative
directors. Auditors, verifiers, judges, and integration engineers provide
checks, evidence, and repair routing; they never become a fourth creative lane.

Durable contracts live in:

- `PARAVOXIA_CREATIVE_COUNCIL.md`
- `main/CINEMATOGRAPHY.md`
- `main/src/story/ux/README.md` (the executable player-guidance context
  contract for objective, marker, HUD, and feedback lifecycles)
- `docs/architecture/workflow-orchestration/examples/paravoxia-creative-triad.workflow.json`
- `.codex/production-runs/_template/`

## Story scope

Post-arrival story work is **authorized**. The owner lifted the post-arrival
gate on 2026-07-28 (recorded at the top of `PARAVOXIA_DEMO_FOUNDATION_PLAN.md`):
story beyond `ch9-hearth` may be designed, built, and registered, including the

# Common Ground — bounded documentation authority re-audit (pass 2, final)

Run `.codex/story-runs/2026-09-06-common-ground` · read-only · no build, no patch, no probe, no runtime pass · scope limited to the exact `implementation-diff.patch` (iteration 2) and the five patched documents

## Verdict: **APPROVE** (documentation-only direction approval)

Every defect the first pass called *blocking* (D1, D2) is now factually repaired in the files themselves, not merely hedged in a banner. D3, D7 and D8 are repaired as filed. D4 is correctly re-dispositioned against the actual signed text, not against the prior reviewer's inference. D5 and D6 are stated as required future preconditions in the exact places a future geometry signer will read. Bounded authorization is unchanged: no candidate, register, signature or owner-delegation artifact moved.

Two residual staleness items remain inside the patched Execution Plan; both are already covered by the new §0 supersession clause and neither is a machine-file misquotation. They are recorded below as non-blocking, not as a reopened cleanup.

---

## 1. Authorization envelope — unchanged (verified)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Candidate identity | `candidateSha256 790b2894…87ae` — identical in `authority-patch-receipt.json`, `check-results.json`, `owner-story-decision.json` and all three signatures |
| Register identity | `decisionsSha256 017bafda…90fd` identical across chapter / score / cinematography signoffs and the owner decision |
| Signature set | Three exact directors, one candidate, one register; `directorSignoffsSha256 a3289ff1…` unchanged |
| Owner decision honesty | `authorityKind: standing-user-delegation`, `personallyReviewedByUser: false`, `runtimeMutationAuthorizedByThisDecision: false`, `publicationAuthorized: false`, `acceptedMissingEvidence: false` — unchanged, still refuses to fabricate personal review |
| Diff scope | Exactly the five documentation paths; 958 source files compared; `unexpectedRuntimeDrift: []`; no `src/**` file, no shipped string touched |
| Gates | `story:authority` 1094 pass, smoke pass, `validate-candidate --owner` 77 pass; `noAudiovisualOrRuntimePassClaim: true` |
| Ceilings | `runtimeStoryCeiling ch10-transit`, `releaseStoryCeiling ch4-arrival` — both unchanged by this patch |
| Locked unknowns | `w7744-return-cause` family still present and explicitly re-asserted as open in Bible ¶ and Exec §0 tail; no A5 spend, no A6 claim, no Worker 9 / third-consciousness / Maker escalation |

The iteration-2 patch changed only documentation text; the candidate's authority surface is byte-identical to the signed one. **Bounded authorization confirmed unchanged.**

*Stated limitation:* my toolset is read-only file access. I did not recompute SHA-256. What I verified is that the recorded hashes are mutually consistent and identical to the iteration-1 values, and that the changed-path set equals `documentationAllowedPaths`.

---

## 2. D1–D8 individual dispositions

**D1 — obsolete arrival-terminal/code claim. REPAIRED. Confirmed.**
`STORY.md:353-357` now reads "Current `storyDirector.ts::tickArrival` records `ch4Arrived` and calls `advanceToBeat('ch4-audit')`; there is no current `completeStory()` or TEMPORARY terminal branch there." Source agrees exactly: `storyDirector.ts:2299-2300` is `markMilestone(STORY_MILESTONES.ch4Arrived); advanceToBeat('ch4-audit');`, and `TEMPORARY`/`completeStory` do not occur in that file. The old title-block "TEMPORARY TERMINAL" paragraph is gone; the "?story=<beat> for EVERY beat" over-claim was correctly narrowed to "the historical first-act entries listed here" (accurate — `storyState.ts:736` shows deep-link params beyond that list). *Accept.*

**D2 — misquoted machine ceiling. REPAIRED. Confirmed.**
Bible §10 (`:1486-1491`) now: "**Status refreshed 2026-09-06** … through `ch10-transit` … The former July 15 `ch9-hearth` ceiling is superseded … **runtime:** `ch10-transit`". Exec Plan §13 (`:1660-1665`) now: "the July 15 core-path checkpoint through `ch9-hearth` is retained below as delivery lineage. The current `story-authority.json` records formal runtime ceiling `ch10-transit`". Both match `story-authority.json:7`. No false quotation of the machine file remains in the five patched docs. *Accept.*

**D3 — inherited grammar divergence. REPAIRED. Confirmed.**
Bible `:100-102`: "The historical rule already diverges from existing post-A4 emergent captions, which remain unchanged; no global voice correction is commissioned." Paired with the §8 amendment at `:1288-1291`, which now labels the blanket ban "Historical blanket rule" and scopes the `CG-D08` exception to new ch13 copy only. The divergence is acknowledged, no shipped copy is rewritten, and no additional speaker is created. *Accept.*

**D4 — sample/length caps. NOT A CONTRACT CONTRADICTION. I independently agree, on the signed text.**
I read the actual signed candidate ¶59 rather than the prior conclusion. It reads: "Storage is one typed, versioned, actor/world-scoped survey snapshot: **at most** two route slots …, 128 grounded samples **and** 120 world units per trace … **At capacity, stop honestly and offer the actual span or revision.**" The governing quantifier is *at most*, the conjunction is two independent maxima, and the contract already specifies the behaviour when one binds before the other — an honest stop with a revision offer, plus the standing "never silently decimate a tested corner." There is no predicate anywhere in the signed text promising that an arbitrary 120-unit trace fits inside 128 samples. The first pass read a conjunction of limits as a joint guarantee; that was an inference, and it is not what was signed.
Cinema confirms this independently and without prompting (`cinema-current-baseline.md:37`): "Both the 128-point and 120-unit caps must be obeyed independently. The measured winding examples reach the point cap sooner; that is a practical route-budget constraint, not permission to raise either cap, promise every 120-unit trace fits, or silently decimate player evidence." The Execution Plan now states the same thing in the pre-geometry paragraph (`:92-94`) with the explicit no-silent-relaxation clause. Caps unchanged, no errata needed, no signature disturbed. *Accept as filed; the earlier "internally infeasible" finding is withdrawn.*

**D5 — outer route class. CLARIFIED as required. Confirmed.**
Bible `:63-66`: "These are required future route classes: the continuous-reference outer route is **not yet established by measurement**. Failure to establish it reopens the bounded arena decision before scene geometry can be signed." Exec Plan `:89-90` and `:96-97` carry the matching statement and reopening condition. This preserves the honest negative from the geometry pass ("unestablished, not proof") while keeping both routes as the contracted design target — the correct distinction between a canon requirement and a measured fact. *Accept.*

**D6 — undefined witness predicate. CLARIFIED as an explicit precondition. Confirmed.**
Exec Plan `:90-91`: "Define the fixed reference and moving instrument socket endpoints/heights before evaluating their actual occlusion." This is stated *ahead of* the geometry signature and is exactly the right ordering: the tolerances in candidate ¶61 remain "candidate" values whose "exact feasibility remains for the scene contract," and the socket/height definition is now a named blocker on that contract rather than a silent gap. Correctly paired with `:94-96`, "Do not require the new unimplemented mechanic's interaction proof at that earlier boundary; verify it after signed implementation" — which honours the pre-geometry meaning you specified (existing physical paths and reference relations, not the unbuilt trace/refusal). *Accept.*

**D7 — receipt-only install. REPAIRED. Confirmed.**
Bible `:22-29` now separates the two things cleanly: "…already perform the station transaction and cell installation, **recording second-hearth restoration by receipt** … The current install consumes the cell and commits receipts; **it has no dedicated habitat-state change, caption or score acknowledgment.**" The future payoff is kept strictly in the direction section and in production order item 1 ("Give the real second-hearth install its bounded acknowledgment"). STORY.md's "installs it at Tidegarden's second hearth" is accurate as an interaction description and is no longer the only account. Present receipt and future payoff are now unambiguously distinct. *Accept.*

**D8 — source pointers and production identity. REPAIRED. Confirmed.**
`src/story/beats/definitions.ts` and `src/story/beats/registry.ts` are added to `runtimeEvidence` in **both** `story-authority.json:31-32` and the schema `const` block; all seven added paths exist on disk (`beats/definitions.ts`, `beats/metadata.generated.ts`, `beats/registry.ts`, `spaceStationStory.ts`, `stationReturnStory.ts`, `StationScreeningDriver.tsx`, `autopilot/primitives.ts`). `runtimeBeatAuthority: "src/story/storyState.ts"` is *correct as-is* — `storyState.ts:79-107` still authors the `StoryBeat` union and `:349` the ordered list; only metadata moved out. Retained production identity is now explicit rather than an apparent oversight: Bible `:1493-1496` "The machine map's older production-contract identity is intentionally retained until the new chapter is implemented and registered through its separate signed scene contract," echoed at Exec Plan `:1665-1666`. *Accept.*

---

## 3. New defects found in this exact diff

**No blocking defect.** Two non-blocking residues, both inside the Execution Plan and both already covered by the new §0 supersession clause. I record them for honesty; I do not recommend gating on them, and neither should trigger a broader old-canon pass.

- **R1 (minor, one line).** `PARAVOXIA_STORY_EXECUTION_PLAN.md:300` (gap register F01) still reads "typed state **now** continues from `ch4-audit` through `ch9-hearth` and `done`". The `ch9-hearth → done` adjacency is stale — `done` now follows `ch10-transit` (`storyState.ts:349-350`). Unlike D2 this is not a quotation of the machine file's ceiling, and §0's table supersedes it explicitly. Smallest fix, whenever F01 is next touched: "…through `ch10-transit` and `done`."
- **R2 (cosmetic).** `PARAVOXIA_STORY_EXECUTION_PLAN.md:224` lists implemented content "from `ch4-audit` through `ch9-hearth`" — accurate as a content enumeration, incomplete as a range. No repair required.
- **Out of scope, noted only:** `PARAVOXIA_EMERGENT_STORY_BATCH_PLAN.md:1746` still asserts the authority map records a `ch9-hearth` runtime ceiling. That file is lineage, is not among the five governing/patched docs, and is not authority over `story-authority.json`. Flagged, not commissioned.

Also verified clean in this diff: no shipped copy string changed; no `ch13` identifier exists anywhere in `main/src` (0 matches), so the "approved direction, not yet implemented" framing is literally true; STORY.md's demo-lock rewrite remains backed by the 2026-07-28 gate lift in `PARAVOXIA_DEMO_FOUNDATION_PLAN.md`; the `completeStory` reference surviving at `STORY.md:236` is still accurate (`emergentStoryDirector.ts:1490`, `storyState.ts:830`).

---

## 4. Preserved distinctions — all intact

- **Docs-only direction approval** vs **scene geometry / hardware / actual-code gates**: held throughout. Bible: "Runtime requires its own signed scene contract." Exec §0: "no runtime implementation or current audiovisual acceptance claimed by this documentation patch," and "Software frames are geometry diagnostics only; final headed hardware and supported-tier evidence remain required."
- **Pre-geometry means existing physical paths and reference relations**, not proof of the unbuilt mechanic — stated correctly and explicitly.
- **Reveal discipline**: nothing in the patch grants Worker 9 survival, the shared body, the third consciousness, W-7744's future motives, alliance or A5. W-7744's outcome remains `PASSAGE OBSERVED. MODEL INCOMPLETE.` — a bounded local tester, explicitly "not a network clearance, friendship, alliance, passenger invitation or awakening installed by Terra."
- **Both-readings integrity** of the approved direction: the reciprocal crossing reads as labour-coercion satire (an auditor forced to hold the other end of his own measurement) and as the AI's biography (a model conceding incompleteness after grounded evidence) without either reading collapsing, and the twist is never stated plainly.

---

## Summary

The goal plot is **structurally safe**. This iteration closes the two present-tense falsehoods that made the first pass a revise, acknowledges the inherited grammar divergence without touching a line of shipped copy, and converts D5/D6 from silent gaps into named preconditions that a future geometry signer must clear. D4 was a reviewer inference and the signed text — "at most … and … per trace," plus "at capacity, stop honestly" — does not carry the promise that was read into it; the caps stand unchanged and un-relaxed, with cinema's independent confirmation on record.

**Single highest-leverage remaining action (non-blocking): carry the same dated-supersession discipline into `PARAVOXIA_STORY_EXECUTION_PLAN.md:300` when F01 is next edited**, so the gap register's own "current truth" column stops disagreeing with §0 four hundred lines above it. Nothing else in this diff should hold the documentation pass.

are still open. This is a scoped answer, not a global resolution.

The player demonstrates a route through the familiar living site by actually
walking it. A bounded survey trace records that proposal. W-7744 tests its
grounded spans and can stop for a specific footing or reference failure. The
player can redraw the untested tail without losing valid work, choose a longer
route he can repeat independently, or use a shorter span requiring an occupied
witness. Both routes are complete choices with different retained geometry and
repeatability; neither receives a moral or musical rank. Council-v2 selects one
new passive, visibly opaque-backed survey instrument with a constant 12-unit
socket-to-socket range. Its visible solids also govern walking collision and
reference occlusion; there is no invisible directional cone. The measured CPU
basis establishes a 16-unit short route with a 14-unit reference shadow and a
fully supported 36-unit long route, with all trace caps retained. This proves
the proposed route-class distinction, not a playable or rendered scene. Exact
connected-head and nonoverlapping actor staging belong to the scene contract;
current terrain edits and live interaction must still be verified.

Both choices require the reversal. Terra first mistakes having crossed for
having finished the proof: `i walked it. i thought that finished the proof.`
Her wanted comparison needs W-7744 to maintain a separate reference while she
moves through the part the fixed instrument cannot support. Actual completion
of that passage earns `i needed the end he held.` She then explicitly offers
and occupies a separate safe far reference. He makes the final grounded test
on his own responsibility under the same live range, solid sight, grounding,
occupancy and body-clearance rules; retained proof is not unlimited sensing. His local entry is
`PASSAGE OBSERVED. MODEL INCOMPLETE.` It is not a network clearance, friendship,
alliance, passenger invitation or awakening installed by Terra. He remains a
bounded local tester on Origin; the route and optional repeat survey persist.
His old A4 departure and lost pack remain true.

The new capacity is relational reading at `alive`: a shared act can preserve
different accounts. Witness validity uses actual world/actor/reference geometry
and occupied position, never camera gaze, waiting, optional foliage density,
music or interpretation. The trace reveals only walked ground. Continuous
drawing keeps one quiet standing instruction, without a prompt or chime for
each point or turn. Range failure, actual solid occlusion, unsafe footing and
temporary reference vacancy remain distinct and reversible. No alternate
renderer, consciousness score or higher reality stage is introduced. First
interstellar warp still owns A5 Light. Worker 9 remains conscious; this chapter
adds no attributed voice, third-consciousness sign, Maker answer or
greater-threat revelation.

The audiovisual direction retains a player-owned embodied view and existing
world palettes. Grounded feet, the trace break and exchanged positions carry
the turn. The hearth's warmth returns first. At Origin, the unresolved audit
square returns; temporary witness holds do not repeatedly restart its phrase.
Only his actually completed test permits changed phrase spacing, without a
victory cadence or alliance theme. Controls return immediately; a live-only
final texture may last at most five seconds before the existing 4.5-second
release fade, with early cancellation and no replay on restore or repeat play.
There is no extra coda, forced camera, new light, postprocessing unlock or
shared audio-engine rewrite.

**Bounded voice clarification (`CG-D08`).** New ch13 sensory or involuntary
thought may remain lowercase and parenthetical; deliberately owned intent is

with strict entry/exit evidence. Do not weaken direct registry adjacency or
   add a restored-home guarantee to ch10. Extend the actual movie departure,
   return flight, landing and cell installation without a `story=` reseed.
3. Build `ch13-home`, `ch13-return`, `ch13-survey`, `ch13-common` through a
   matching production lock and signed scene contract. Use chapter-local
   state/director/world/beat/rail modules and one integrator for shared owners.
4. Implement the actual walked trace, reversible tested-prefix/untested-tail
   rules, two durable route classes, world-position witness hysteresis,
   reciprocal crossing and W-7744's grounded independent test. Retain a bounded
   local actor and optional repeat survey after completion. Existing
   observation-ledger entries remain non-gating.
5. Bind world/actor-scoped versioned persistence, resume/deep-link/reset,
   objective/marker/F arbitration and one-shot semantic feedback. Preserve
   unrelated dirty files, especially live beat/autopilot and audio work.
6. Realize the accepted score and embodied staging through existing camera,
   material, lighting and score authorities. No new shared audio graph, light
   topology, world generation or alternate renderer is commissioned.

The council's measured geometry basis selects a 12-unit reference range and a
single passive backed instrument. The short route is 16 units with a 14-unit
housing shadow; the fixed-reference-supported longer route is 36 units (61
samples), 20 units and 125 percent longer. The common 18-unit passage has full
held-reference coverage and a real eight-unit contiguous portion outside the
fixed reference's useful coverage. The two route classes are therefore grounded
in CPU evidence; no playable, rendered or hardware result is implied.

The scene contract must bind the final connected head and separate near-end
body positions: Terra cannot start inside the worker who holds her reference.
After her actual comparison she explicitly offers and occupies the separate
far reference for his independently initiated test. All current range, solid
sight, grounding, occupancy and body-clearance rules remain active throughout.
The tested survey class and her earned comparison are separate saved facts.

Both independent caps (128 samples and 120 walked units) apply simultaneously;
a winding path may hit the point cap first. Neither cap may be silently relaxed
or a tested corner decimated. Keep one quiet instruction while tracing and
distinguish range, solid, footing and temporary vacancy holds. Exact scene
placement is bound before runtime; new interaction, day/night, actual terrain
edits, supported-tier and headed hardware proof follows signed implementation.

Acceptance is the run's `implementation-acceptance.md`: existing restored and
pending-cell saves; actual continuous station-to-home-to-ch13 play; three cold
movies with no timeout rescue; both route choices and their distinct saved
repeatability; physical/reference refusal, revision and witness recovery;
W-7744's necessary reciprocal contribution and real final arrival; correct
objective/prompt/marker/feedback lifecycles; full verification; bounded audio

# Critic Report — ranked findings

Each finding gives evidence, why it matters, the smallest responsible repair boundary, who decides, and the retest. I route; I do not repair.

---

**1. (Medium, accepted) The chapter's central promise rests on a premise the packet itself labels unestablished.**
- *Evidence:* Candidate ¶17 asserts "Both are complete solutions"; Bible addendum: "the continuous-reference outer route is **not yet established by measurement**. Failure to establish it reopens the bounded arena decision"; `geometry-feasibility.json` pass 1 produced one dry route pair under a blanket 3.0-unit near-field exemption and a ray method the packet itself later characterises as unreliable; `alignment-report.md` §4: "one source-derived dry route under its sampled witness assumptions, not both designed route classes."
- *Why it matters:* "Two complete solutions with different persistence and no moral rank" is the chapter's entire agency proposition. If only one route class exists, the mechanic collapses into an escort with a cosmetic alternative, and the reciprocal reversal — the thematic payoff — loses its second reading.
- *Smallest boundary:* none in this candidate. It is already conditioned, and reopening is already the declared consequence. Do not pre-empt it in documentation.
- *Decision:* director-level (cinematography + chapter) on the measurement; **owner** only if the arena must be reopened or moved.
- *Retest:* independent verification of the geometry stream against shipped conventions (rendered-cube gate, voxel-centre AABB, real socket heights, trunk collider), then both route classes, distinct witness dependence, and day/night legibility — before any exact scene-layout signature.

**2. (Low) A stale present-tense "Current truth" row survives inside a just-patched governing document.**
- *Evidence:* `main/PARAVOXIA_STORY_EXECUTION_PLAN.md:300` (F01): "typed state **now** continues from `ch4-audit` through `ch9-hearth` and `done`" — verified by me against `storyState.ts:349–350`, where `done` follows `ch10-transit`. Recorded by the documentation auditor as R1 and left as "non-blocking".
- *Why it matters:* this is the exact defect class (D2) the iteration-2 patch was commissioned to close. §0's supersession clause covers it in principle, but a table column literally headed *Current truth* is where a future reader looks first. Judgement law 1 is literal.
- *Smallest boundary:* one line — "…through `ch10-transit` and `done`". Nothing else in F01, no broader gap-register pass.
- *Decision:* documentation-patch engineer under existing delegation; no owner decision required.

`sha256(story-authority-candidate.md) = 133d1dbe…2cbf`, byte-equal to the
